Hi all —

I've reviewed Acme's redlines. High-level: most items are standard but there are three sticking points that will require either redlines accepted by Acme or an internal exception:

1) Data transfer mechanism: Acme is requesting vendor-managed SCCs. We support SCCs via an Addendum but our standard is to retain jurisdiction/choice-of-law in our DPA; Acme's draft pushes to their local jurisdiction. We can propose a narrow change: EU SCC Addendum + choice-of-law in CA, with a mutual cooperation clause.

2) Subprocessors & audit rights: Acme has expanded audit language and immediate notice requirements for new subprocessors. We'll provide the full subprocessors list, but we will need to limit audit rights to scope-based assessments (SOC2/ISO) rather than on-site audits.

3) Data deletion/retention: Acme is asking for aggressive deletion timelines that conflict with our standard backup and legal hold processes. We can offer a 90-day deletion window post-termination, with exceptions for legal holds.

If Acme will accept those points, I think we can get to sign-off quickly. Otherwise we need a documented risk exception for deviation on jurisdiction and on on-site audit clause. Vivek — pls advise on whether the 90-day deletion + SOC2 evidence is acceptable from a security standpoint or if you need additional controls.

Rishi
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Nguyen <sophie.nguyen@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-10-03T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Redlines and e-signature plan

Thanks Rishi —

A few clarifications from procurement:
- Procurement will accept a vendor Addendum with the EU SCCs only if the contract explicitly commits to the SCC terms (not just a reference).
- On-site audits are rare but procurement wants the language to allow scoped assessments at their discretion; if you can commit to scoped third-party assessments and tighter notice, that would be helpful.
- The board will not approve exceptions for jurisdiction language without an exec-level security sign-off.

Procurement also reiterated the Oct 6 doc sign deadline. If Redwood can provide: (a) finalized DPA that includes the SCC Addendum language, (b) subprocessors list, and (c) SOC2 evidence by EOD Oct 5, they will prepare the DocuSign envelope.

Attached: Acme's cover note (no redline).

Sophie
